subject: Taxes
title: The Russian Revolution's Tax Roots
description: A quick, practical guide to The Russian Revolution's Tax Roots.

hook.text: Russia's 1917 revolution had tax roots. Peasants paid crushing 'redemption payments' for land they thought was theirs.

buildup.text: After serfdom ended in 1861, peasants had to buy their own land from nobles through 49 years of government payments.

discovery.text: Redemption payments consumed 25% of peasant income.

twist.text: The Bolsheviks promised 'land, bread, and peace.' Ending unjust taxes was central to winning peasant support.

climax.text: Russia shows that tax systems that feel like punishment create revolutionary conditions over generations.

punchline.text: 49 years of payments for your own land. Revolution was brewing.

quiz.question: What were 'redemption payments' in Russia?
options: Payments peasants made to buy their own land after serfdom ended
